scenes.title: A Journey Across India
narration: Have you ever traveled to a big city in India by train?
India is huge, with many bustling cities that are special in their own way.
Let us explore four famous cities that tell a story of our country.

scenes.title: Capital and Financial Hubs
narration: New Delhi is our capital city where the government works.
Mumbai is famous as the financial hub and for its busy ports.
In these cities, millions of people live, work, and dream every day.

scenes.title: Tech and Cultural Centers
narration: Bengaluru is known as the Garden City and the hub of technology.
Kolkata is famous for its rich history, literature, and beautiful festivals.
Imagine taking a metro train in Bengaluru or visiting a library in Kolkata.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Kolkata show India's diversity.
Each city has unique jobs, buildings, and traditions that make it special.
If you could visit any city in India tomorrow, which one would you pick?

scenes.title: A Map of Many States
narration: Have you ever traveled across our big country, India, on a train?
India is divided into many states to help us govern it easily.
Did you know that every single state has its own special capital city?

scenes.title: What is a Capital?
narration: A capital city is the main center where the state government works.
It is like the brain of the state, making important decisions for everyone.
Governors and Chief Ministers often work from offices in these capital cities.

scenes.title: Let's Visit Karnataka
narration: Let us take a trip to the beautiful state of Karnataka in the south.
The capital city of Karnataka is Bengaluru, known for its parks and technology.
In Bengaluru, the state assembly meets at the famous Vidhana Soudha building.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Remember, India has many states, and each state has exactly one capital city.
These cities manage laws and services that help our communities grow.
Can you find out the name of the capital city of your home state today?

scenes.title: What are Union Territories
narration: Have you seen a map of India with its 28 states and 8 special territories?
These 8 places are called Union Territories, managed directly by the central government.
Unlike states, they do not have their own state governments to run daily tasks.

scenes.title: Why are they special
narration: Some territories are small, like the beautiful city of Chandigarh.
Others are far away in the ocean, like the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Their small size or distance makes them special for national security and history.

scenes.title: Names of the Territories
narration: Delhi is our capital territory, and Puducherry is famous for its history.
Lakshadweep and Daman and Diu are coastal spots with blue water.
Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli complete our list.

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: India has 8 Union Territories governed by the central government in New Delhi.
They are diverse, from snowy mountains in the north to tropical islands.
Can you find these 8 territories on your school classroom map today?

scenes.title: The Journey of Rivers
narration: Have you ever wondered where the water in our taps comes from?
Rivers start high up in the mountains as melting snow.
They flow down through valleys, getting wider as they travel.

scenes.title: What are Dams?
narration: Sometimes, we build a big wall across a river called a dam.
Dams hold back river water to create a giant lake.
We use this water for drinking and watering our farms.
Dams also help us make electricity for our homes.

scenes.title: A Famous Example
narration: Let us look at the Bhakra Nangal Dam in Himachal Pradesh.
It is built on the Sutlej River to help people nearby.
This dam provides water to many fields in Punjab and Haryana.

scenes.title: Recap and Thinking
narration: Rivers give us water, and dams help us store it safely.
Dams are useful for farming and making clean energy.
Think about it: Why do you think we need to save water?

scenes.title: What Are National Parks?
narration: Have you ever visited a forest and wondered who keeps the animals safe?
National parks are special protected areas where nature is kept exactly as it should be.
These places keep our wild animals and trees away from harm and busy cities.

scenes.title: Why Protect Our Wildlife?
narration: Every animal plays a role in keeping our environment healthy and balanced.
Some parks are created to save animals that are becoming very rare in the wild.
By visiting these parks, we learn to respect and cherish India's incredible natural beauty.

scenes.title: The Famous Kaziranga Park
narration: Let us look at Kaziranga National Park in Assam, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros.
These rhinos roam freely in the tall grasslands, protected by park rangers day and night.
Visitors can take a jeep safari to see these majestic creatures from a safe distance.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: National parks are safe homes that protect India's amazing wildlife and beautiful forests.
Remember, when you visit, always follow the rules to keep the animals happy.
Think about it: which animal would you love to see in its natural home?

scenes.title: What is a Sanctuary
narration: Have you ever seen a tiger or an elephant in a deep forest?
A wildlife sanctuary is a safe home where animals roam freely without fear.
Why do these animals need special protected places to live?

scenes.title: Keeping Animals Safe
narration: Sanctuaries provide food, water, and shelter for endangered animals.
Humans are not allowed to hunt or harm animals inside these areas.
Forest officers work hard to keep the habitat clean and peaceful.
These zones help plants and animals grow together in balance.

scenes.title: A Famous Example
narration: Let us visit the Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary in Kerala.
It is famous for the beautiful Periyar Lake located inside the forest.
You can spot wild elephants drinking water near the lake shore.
Many unique birds and tall trees also make this their home.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Sanctuaries protect animals and keep our forests healthy and green.
They are special places where nature is respected and preserved.
If you could visit one sanctuary in India, which animal would you hope to see?

scenes.title: A Journey Through History
narration: Have you ever seen a building that looks like a giant palace from a storybook?
These are called monuments, and they tell us stories about India's past.
Let's travel across our beautiful country to visit some famous ones today.

scenes.title: Learning About Famous Monuments
narration: The Taj Mahal in Agra is a beautiful white marble tomb built long ago.
It was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in the 1600s.
It is famous for its perfect shape and beautiful carvings on the walls.

scenes.title: More Wonders of India
narration: The Qutub Minar in Delhi is a very tall tower made of red stone.
In the south, the Hampi ruins show us how grand the Vijayanagara Empire was.
These places are protected to keep our history safe for everyone.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Monuments are special buildings that help us remember people and events from long ago.
From the Taj Mahal to Hampi, they show us the skill of ancient builders.
Think about it: which monument would you like to visit with your family first?

scenes.title: The Big Globe Hook
narration: Have you ever looked at a globe and wondered why the land is split into big chunks?
There is so much water, but these huge land masses are where we all live.
Today, let's travel across the seven continents that make up our amazing planet.

scenes.title: Understanding The Idea
narration: A continent is a very large area of land surrounded mostly by water.
We have seven of them, and each one has its own special geography and weather.
Scientists call these massive pieces of land continents, and they cover all our countries.

scenes.title: Example: Asia and Others
narration: Look at Asia, our own continent, which is the largest one on Earth.
Next is Africa, known for its vast deserts and incredible wildlife.
Then we have North America, South America, Europe, Australia, and icy Antarctica.
Each one sits on a giant plate of rock moving slowly beneath us.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: Remember, we have seven continents, and Asia is where India is located.
They are all separated by vast oceans that keep our world diverse and unique.
Think about it: If you could visit any continent tomorrow, which one would you choose?

scenes.title: A World of Many Countries
narration: Have you ever looked at a globe and wondered why there are so many different colors?
Each color represents a different country with its own special land and people.
Every country has one main city called a capital city where the government works.

scenes.title: What Makes a Capital Special
narration: A capital is like the heart of the country, helping make important rules and decisions.
It is often where you find big monuments, museums, and important historical buildings.
Sometimes, the capital is the busiest and most famous city in the whole land.

scenes.title: Example: New Delhi, India
narration: Let us look at our home country, India, and its capital city, New Delhi.
New Delhi is where the President and Prime Minister of India work every day.
Famous places like the India Gate are located right there in the capital.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Remember, every country has one capital city that acts as its administrative center.
Capitals are special places that hold the history and laws of their nations.
Think about it: If you were to design a capital city, what important building would you put first?

scenes.title: What are Heritage Sites?
narration: Have you ever visited a super old fort or a famous temple in India?
These special places are protected because they tell us stories about our history.
UNESCO helps look after these treasures so everyone can enjoy them forever.

scenes.title: Why do they matter?
narration: Heritage sites can be beautiful buildings, ancient caves, or even large national parks.
They show how people lived, built homes, and prayed hundreds of years ago.
Keeping them safe means our culture stays alive for the next generation.

scenes.title: The Taj Mahal Example
narration: The Taj Mahal in Agra is a famous UNESCO site made of white marble.
It was finished in 1653 and is known for its perfect shape and carvings.
People visit from all over the world to see its grand beauty.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Heritage sites are protected treasures that show us our amazing Indian history.
From the Taj Mahal to Kaziranga, these places connect us to our past.
Think about it: which historical site in your own state would you like to visit?

scenes.title: The Big Blue Question
narration: Have you ever looked at a globe and noticed how much of it is covered in blue?
That blue represents our vast oceans, but do you know how many there are?
Let us dive in and explore the five giant oceans on our Earth.

scenes.title: Naming the Big Five
narration: First is the Pacific, which is the largest and deepest ocean of them all.
Next is the Atlantic, followed by the chilly Indian Ocean near our home.
Finally, we have the Southern Ocean and the frozen Arctic Ocean up north.

scenes.title: Oceans in Our Lives
narration: Think of the Indian Ocean that touches the coastline of beautiful India.
It helps ships carry goods like tea and electronics to different parts of the world.
It also gives us rain and is home to many amazing sea creatures.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: We have five oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic.
These oceans connect the whole world and keep our planet healthy.
Think about it: Why is it important for us to keep our oceans clean?

scenes.title: What are mountains?
narration: Have you ever looked at a giant hill reaching into the clouds?
Mountains are massive parts of Earth that rise high above everything else.
They are much taller and steeper than regular hills.

scenes.title: How mountains are made
narration: Deep under our feet, the Earth is made of giant moving plates.
When these giant plates push against each other, the land folds up.
This slow squeeze creates the tall, rocky shapes we call mountains.

scenes.title: Example: The Himalayas
narration: The Himalayas are the tallest mountain range in the whole world.
Mount Everest is the highest peak found right in this range.
These mountains act like a giant wall that stops cold winds.

scenes.title: Mountains Recap
narration: Mountains are tall, rocky, and formed by moving plates over millions of years.
They change the weather and are home to special plants and animals.
Think about it: if you climbed a mountain, what things would you pack?

scenes.title: A Land Without Rain
narration: Have you ever seen a place where it almost never rains?
Deserts are places that get very little water each year.
Some deserts are hot like the Sahara, while others are freezing cold.

scenes.title: How Life Survives
narration: Plants and animals must be smart to live in the dry heat.
Cactus plants store water inside their thick stems for long dry spells.
Many animals only come out at night when the air is cooler.

scenes.title: The Thar Desert Story
narration: In India, we have the beautiful Thar Desert in Rajasthan.
Look at the rolling sand dunes stretching across the land.
People there wear bright colors and live near small water holes.

scenes.title: Remembering Desert Facts
narration: Deserts are dry places that can be hot or very cold.
Plants and animals have special ways to save water.
Think about it, what would you bring to survive in a desert?

scenes.title: Why Rivers Matter
narration: Have you ever wondered where the water in your tap comes from?
Rivers are like nature's highways carrying water across the land.
They provide water for drinking, farming, and homes everywhere.

scenes.title: How Rivers Flow
narration: Rivers usually start as tiny streams high up in the mountains.
As they flow down, they join other streams to get bigger.
Finally, most rivers travel a long way to reach the big ocean.

scenes.title: Famous Rivers Around Us
narration: In India, the holy Ganga is our longest and most beloved river.
The Nile in Africa is often called the longest river on Earth.
The Amazon in South America holds the most water of any river.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Rivers start in mountains, grow larger, and flow to the sea.
They support life, farming, and our daily water needs.
Can you name a river near your town or city?

scenes.title: The Wonder Of Landmarks
narration: Have you ever wondered why people travel across the world to see certain special places?
These famous sites are called landmarks, and they tell us stories about history and culture.
Let's explore some incredible landmarks that make our world so unique.

scenes.title: Famous Global Sites
narration: In India, the Taj Mahal in Agra is a beautiful landmark made of white marble.
The Great Wall of China is a massive stone structure that stretches for thousands of miles.
In France, the Eiffel Tower stands tall over the city of Paris.
The Statue of Liberty in the USA is a giant symbol of friendship and freedom.

scenes.title: Why Landmarks Matter
narration: Landmarks are important because they remind us of how people lived long ago.
They also show us the amazing things humans can build with clever tools and hard work.
Protecting these sites helps future generations learn about our shared human story.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Today we learned that landmarks are famous, historic places found all across the globe.
From the Taj Mahal to the Great Wall, every landmark has a special story to tell.
Think about it: If you could build a new landmark in your city, what would it look like?

scenes.title: A Mysterious Discovery
narration: Have you ever found an old treasure buried in your garden?
Long ago, near the Indus River, people built a huge city.
Archaeologists dug deep to find these hidden homes.

scenes.title: Smart City Planning
narration: They built straight streets that crossed like a grid.
They even had covered drains to keep the city clean.
Houses were made of strong, baked bricks.

scenes.title: Trade and Daily Life
narration: People traded colorful beads and pretty pottery.
Farmers grew wheat and barley in the fertile soil.
They used special seals to mark their goods.

scenes.title: Remembering the Past
narration: The Indus Valley was one of the world's first civilizations.
They taught us how to build cities and trade.
If you built a city, what important invention would you add?

scenes.title: A Powerful Ancient Kingdom
narration: Have you ever seen the four lions on our Indian coins and notes?
That symbol comes from a very famous empire called the Mauryan Empire.
Do you wonder how one ruler managed such a huge land long ago?

scenes.title: Building the Empire
narration: Chandragupta Maurya started the empire with the help of his clever teacher, Chanakya.
They built a strong army to unite many small kingdoms into one.
They also created a system to collect taxes and keep the people safe.

scenes.title: The Story of Ashoka
narration: Ashoka the Great was the most famous ruler of this powerful dynasty.
After a big battle, he felt sad about the fighting and chose peace instead.
He carved messages of kindness on stone pillars all across his kingdom.

scenes.title: Remembering the Mauryas
narration: The Mauryas taught us about unity, peaceful living, and good government.
Their symbols still remind us of our history every time we use money.
Think about it: Why do you think peace is better than fighting a war?

scenes.title: Sunlight and Our Clock
narration: Have you ever wondered why your cousin in London wakes up while you are sleeping?
Our Earth is like a giant ball spinning in space.
As it turns, the Sun lights up only one side at a time.

scenes.title: How Time Zones Work
narration: We divide the world into twenty-four slices called time zones.
Each zone represents one hour of the day.
When the Sun is high in Delhi, it is still early morning elsewhere.

scenes.title: A Global Example
narration: Let us imagine it is noon in India.
If you travel far west, the time goes backward.
In London, it would be early morning because the Sun has not reached them yet.

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: The Earth spins, creating day and night across the globe.
Time zones help us track the Sun's position everywhere.
Think about it: if you could fly around the world in an hour, would your watch stay the same?

scenes.title: A Royal Hook
narration: Have you ever visited the beautiful Red Fort in Delhi?
It was built long ago by the powerful Mughal emperors.
Do you wonder how they ruled such a vast land?

scenes.title: The Mughal Story
narration: In 1526, Babur came from the north to start the empire.
His grandson, Akbar the Great, was famous for being very fair.
He treated all people with kindness, no matter their religion.
They built many grand palaces and gardens across India.

scenes.title: A Famous Example
narration: Think of the Taj Mahal in Agra, built by Shah Jahan.
He used white marble and precious stones to make it shine.
It still stands today as a symbol of love and history.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: The Mughals ruled for over three hundred years in India.
They left behind amazing forts, tombs, and beautiful art.
Think about it: If you were an emperor, what would you build?

scenes.title: A Time of Treasures
narration: Have you ever wondered why we call ancient India a land of gold?
Long ago, the Gupta Empire ruled over much of northern India.
It was a time when science, art, and learning truly blossomed.

scenes.title: Learning about the Guptas
narration: Chandragupta I was the first great ruler who started this powerful empire.
The kings helped people build beautiful temples and universities.
They also made coins out of pure gold to trade with others.
People lived happily and shared knowledge across the vast lands.

scenes.title: Science and Math Wonders
narration: A brilliant thinker named Aryabhata discovered that Earth spins on its axis.
He also helped perfect the use of the number zero in math.
Doctors learned to heal people using ancient medicinal plants.
Poets wrote famous stories that we still read today.

scenes.title: Why it Matters Today
narration: The Gupta period gave India many inventions we use today.
It was a golden age because of art, math, and peace.
Think about it: which invention from long ago do you use every day?

scenes.title: Welcome to the Medieval Era
narration: Have you ever wondered who built the grand forts in India long ago?
The medieval period was a time of kings, queens, and beautiful new cities.
It started around the year 700 and lasted until 1750.

scenes.title: Kings and Their Kingdoms
narration: Many powerful dynasties ruled different parts of our country.
The Cholas ruled in the south and built amazing stone temples.
The Delhi Sultans and the Mughals built massive walls and gardens.
These rulers helped trade grow across land and sea routes.

scenes.title: Life in the Mughal Times
narration: Let us look at the Mughal Emperor Akbar, who lived in the 1500s.
He encouraged artists to paint colorful pictures of court life.
People wore silk clothes and ate delicious spices like cardamom and cloves.
They used silver rupees as money to buy things at the market.

scenes.title: Looking Back at History
narration: Medieval India gave us beautiful forts, temples, and rich traditions.
History helps us understand how our ancestors lived every single day.
Think about it: If you built a monument today, what would you name it?

scenes.title: A Look at History
narration: Have you ever wondered why we learn about the British in our history books?
Long ago, traders came to India from Britain to buy spices and cloth.
Soon, the East India Company started controlling parts of our land.

scenes.title: Life Under British Rule
narration: The British built long railway lines to move goods across India quickly.
They changed how schools worked and introduced the English language to many students.
But, many Indians felt they were not being treated fairly by the rulers.

scenes.title: The Fight for Freedom
narration: People like Mahatma Gandhi led peaceful protests to demand our freedom back.
Sardar Patel helped unite all the different princely states into one big country.
After many years of struggle, India finally became independent in 1947.

scenes.title: Remembering the Past
narration: The British rule changed India's transport, schools, and laws forever.
We honor the brave leaders who fought to make India free again.
Think about it: How would your life be different if India was never ruled by them?

scenes.title: The Head of India
narration: Have you seen our national flag flying high at schools and parks?
The President is the first citizen of India and our country's head.
Ever wondered what the President actually does for us?

scenes.title: Understanding the Role
narration: The President lives in a beautiful home in New Delhi called Rashtrapati Bhavan.
They sign important laws that help keep our country fair and safe.
The President is also the Supreme Commander of our armed forces.
They represent India when meeting leaders from other countries across the world.

scenes.title: Example of Service
narration: On Republic Day, the President attends a grand parade in New Delhi.
They hoist the flag to celebrate our strong Constitution.
The President also gives special awards to brave children for their courage.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: So, the President is our head, lives in Rashtrapati Bhavan, and signs our laws.
They also lead our defense forces and celebrate our special national days.
Think about it: if you were President, what is one good rule you would make?

scenes.title: Why Do We Have Rules?
narration: Have you ever played a game without any rules?
Everything becomes messy and unfair very quickly.
Just like games, our country India needs a big rulebook too.

scenes.title: What is the Constitution?
narration: This special rulebook is called the Constitution of India.
It tells us how our government works and keeps things fair.
It protects the rights of every citizen living in our land.

scenes.title: How it Works
narration: Imagine Dr. B.R. Ambedkar led the team that wrote it.
They finished this great task in 1949.
It officially started working on 26th January 1950.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Rules
narration: The Constitution is the highest law in India.
It keeps us united and protects our freedom.
Think about it: Why is it important for everyone to follow the same rules?

scenes.title: Life Under British Rule
narration: Have you ever wondered why we celebrate Independence Day on August 15th every year?
Long ago, India was ruled by the British, and we did not have our own government.
Many brave people worked together to help India become a free country.

scenes.title: Leaders of the Movement
narration: Mahatma Gandhi taught people to use non-violence, which means fighting without hurting others.
Sardar Patel worked hard to unite all the different states of India into one nation.
Leaders like Subhash Chandra Bose inspired many to join the struggle for our rights.

scenes.title: The Salt March Example
narration: The British made a law saying Indians had to pay money for salt.
Gandhi ji led a long walk to the ocean to make his own salt.
This showed that Indians would stand up for what is fair and right.

scenes.title: Freedom and Responsibility
narration: In 1947, India finally became an independent nation with its own flag.
Today, we remember our heroes who sacrificed so much for our freedom.
Think about it: how can you be a good citizen in our free India today?

scenes.title: What is the Supreme Court?
narration: Have you ever wondered who decides the rules when people disagree?
In India, the Supreme Court is the highest court in the land.
It is located in our capital city, New Delhi.

scenes.title: How the Court Works
narration: The court acts like a referee for the whole country.
The head of the court is called the Chief Justice of India.
Other judges help to interpret our Constitution.
They ensure everyone is treated fairly by the law.

scenes.title: A Real Life Example
narration: Imagine a factory builds a wall that blocks a public road.
The people go to the local court, but the issue continues.
Finally, the Supreme Court hears the case to protect the public path.
The court orders the wall removed so everyone can walk freely.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: The Supreme Court is India's highest judicial power.
It protects our rights and guides our laws.
Think about it: Why is it important to have one final place to settle big arguments?

scenes.title: The Big House of Laws
narration: Have you ever wondered who makes the rules for our big country, India?
It happens in a special place in New Delhi called the Parliament House.
The Parliament is where leaders meet to talk about what our country needs.

scenes.title: Two Houses of Parliament
narration: The Parliament has two main parts called Houses.
The first is the Lok Sabha, the House of the People.
The second is the Rajya Sabha, the Council of States.
Members are chosen to represent all the people living in India.

scenes.title: Turning Ideas into Laws
narration: Imagine we want a new rule, like keeping our parks cleaner.
A leader writes this idea down as a proposal called a Bill.
Both Houses discuss and vote on it to see if it is good.
Once approved, it becomes a law for the whole country to follow.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Parliament makes our laws in two houses, the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
Leaders work together here to help every state and citizen in India.
Think about it: If you were a leader, what new law would you suggest?

scenes.title: The Big Question
narration: Have you ever wondered who makes sure our big country, India, runs smoothly?
We see the news and hear about the Prime Minister, but what do they really do?
Let us discover how this important role helps every one of us.

scenes.title: What is the Role?
narration: The Prime Minister is the head of the government in India.
They are chosen by the people through elections held across all states.
They lead the Council of Ministers to make big decisions for the nation.

scenes.title: Working for India
narration: Imagine the Prime Minister planning a new school or a hospital for a village.
They work to improve facilities like roads, water supply, and electricity for everyone.
They also represent India at meetings with leaders from other countries.

scenes.title: Summary and Reflection
narration: The Prime Minister leads our government, serves the people, and helps India grow.
They are a vital part of our democracy, elected to serve the nation.
Think about it: If you were Prime Minister, what would you do for your school?

scenes.title: Who Runs Our State
narration: Have you ever wondered who makes the rules for our state, like building schools or fixing roads?
Every state in India has its own government to help people live happily and safely.
Just like a captain leads a team, leaders in our state work together to solve problems.

scenes.title: The Legislative Assembly
narration: The main place where decisions happen is called the Legislative Assembly, or Vidhan Sabha.
People from our area vote for a representative called an MLA to speak for us.
MLAs meet here to discuss new laws that help our schools, hospitals, and parks.

scenes.title: The Chief Minister's Role
narration: The leader of the majority party becomes the Chief Minister of the state.
Think of the Chief Minister like the head of a giant team managing the state's budget.
They choose a group of ministers to look after different departments like health or education.

scenes.title: Working Together For Us
narration: The state government works hard to keep our water clean, our electricity running, and our roads smooth.
By working together, they ensure every citizen in the state gets the help they need.
Think about it: If you were an MLA, what is the first thing you would fix in your town?

scenes.title: Why streets are clean
narration: Have you ever wondered who makes sure our park swings are safe and streets are clean?
It is not just magic, it is your local government working hard for our town.
Let us discover how they keep our daily life running smoothly in India.

scenes.title: The Local Council Team
narration: In big cities, we have a Municipal Corporation to look after things.
In smaller towns, we call this group a Municipal Council.
People choose leaders called Councilors to represent them in meetings.
These leaders make important decisions about taxes and city repairs.

scenes.title: A Day in Our Town
narration: Imagine a broken street light near your house in Bengaluru or Jaipur.
You tell your Councilor, and they bring it up in the town meeting.
The local government then sends workers to fix the light quickly.
This ensures your path to school is bright and safe every evening.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: Local government manages parks, lights, and cleanliness in our local area.
Elected councilors represent us and help solve problems in the community.
Think about it: what is one thing you would improve in your neighborhood today?

scenes.title: Why Rules Matter for Everyone
narration: Have you ever wondered why we follow rules at school and home?
Rules keep us safe and help everyone play fairly together.
In India, our Constitution gives everyone special rules called Fundamental Rights.

scenes.title: Understanding Our Important Rights
narration: The Right to Equality means everyone is treated the same by law.
The Right to Freedom lets us speak, move, and learn freely.
The Right against Exploitation protects children from working in unsafe places.
The Right to Education ensures every child can go to school.

scenes.title: Rights in Action
narration: Imagine Rohan and Priya are both studying in a government school.
Because of the Right to Education, they both get books and bags.
Even if they speak different languages, they have the same rights.

scenes.title: Recapping Our Special Rights
narration: Fundamental Rights protect us, keep us equal, and help us learn.
These rights belong to every citizen in our great country, India.
Think about it: Why is it important to respect others' rights too?

scenes.title: The Body's Curious Questions
narration: Have you ever wondered how you run, jump, and play all day long?
Your body is like a super-smart machine working inside you right now.
Let us look at the three big systems that keep you going.

scenes.title: Bones, Lungs, and Brain
narration: First, your skeleton gives your body shape and protects your soft parts.
Next, your lungs pull in fresh air so you can breathe easily.
Finally, your brain is the boss that tells every part what to do.

scenes.title: How We Play Cricket
narration: Think about a cricket match in your local park.
Your brain sees the ball and tells your muscles to swing the bat.
Your lungs work faster to give you energy to run between the wickets.
Your bones support your weight as you sprint across the field.

scenes.title: Keeping Your Body Healthy
narration: Remember, your skeleton, lungs, and brain work as a team every single day.
To stay strong, eat healthy food, drink water, and get plenty of sleep.
Think about it: which part of your body do you think works hardest while you sleep?

scenes.title: A Look at the Sky
narration: Have you ever looked up at the night sky and wondered about those twinkling lights?
Our sun is actually a giant star at the center of our neighborhood called the solar system.
Eight planets travel in paths around the sun, just like a grand dance in space.

scenes.title: The Inner Planets
narration: The four planets closest to the sun are rocky and small, like Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.
Earth is special because it has water and air, which helps life grow here.
Mars is known as the Red Planet because its soil looks like rust.

scenes.title: The Giant Outer Planets
narration: Further out, we find massive gas giants like Jupiter and Saturn, which are very large.
Saturn is famous for its beautiful rings made of ice and rock pieces.
The furthest planets, Uranus and Neptune, are very cold because they are far from the sun.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: The sun is the center, with four rocky planets inside and four gas giants outside.
Every planet moves in its own path around the sun in perfect rhythm.
If you could visit any planet, which one would you pick and why?

Science and Technology: Chemistry Around.topic: Science and Technology: Chemistry Around Us
Science and Technology: Chemistry Around.title: Chemistry In Your Kitchen

scenes.title: The Magic of Mixtures
narration: Have you ever wondered why milk changes when you add cocoa powder?
It happens because of a science called chemistry.
Chemistry is the study of what things are made of.

scenes.title: Atoms and Molecules
narration: Everything around us is built from tiny blocks called atoms.
When atoms join together, they form molecules.
Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen molecules.

scenes.title: A Kitchen Experiment
narration: Let us look at making a fizzy lemon drink.
We mix lemon juice with baking soda.
The fizz is a new gas being created.
This is a chemical reaction changing the ingredients.

scenes.title: Summary and Thinking
narration: Chemistry is everywhere from the food we eat to the air we breathe.
Remember, atoms make molecules, and reactions create new things.
Think about it: what other changes happen in your kitchen every day?

scenes.title: Who are these scientists?
narration: Have you ever wondered how we get electricity or how rockets reach space?
Scientists are people who solve big puzzles by asking questions and testing ideas.
They use tools and experiments to learn how the world around us works.

scenes.title: Great minds of India
narration: Sir C.V. Raman discovered how light scatters, helping us understand the blue sky.
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was a great scientist who helped build India's powerful rockets.
Dr. Janaki Ammal studied plants to help India grow better crops for our food.

scenes.title: Let us experiment
narration: Imagine you want to see if a seed grows faster with more sunlight.
First, you plant two seeds in identical pots with the same soil and water.
Then, place one in the sun and one in the shade to compare them.
By watching them for a week, you have acted just like a scientist!

scenes.title: Becoming a future scientist
narration: Scientists observe, test, and learn from their mistakes to find the truth.
India needs curious young minds like yours to solve problems for tomorrow.
What is one thing you want to discover in our world today?

scenes.title: A World Without Light
narration: Have you ever wondered how people lived before we had electric light bulbs?
Imagine trying to read your favorite storybook by just a tiny candle flame.
Inventions are clever tools that solve problems and make our daily lives much easier.

scenes.title: Thomas Edison's Bright Idea
narration: Thomas Edison did not invent the first light, but he made a bulb that worked.
He tested thousands of materials to find a wire that would glow without burning.
Finally, in 1879, he found a carbon filament that stayed bright for hours.

scenes.title: From Bulb to Modern India
narration: Think about your home in Delhi or Mumbai today, filled with bright electric lights.
We use this light to study, work, and stay safe after the sun goes down.
Because of this invention, we can keep our schools and hospitals open all night.

scenes.title: Think Like an Inventor
narration: Inventions start with a curious mind and the courage to keep trying.
Remember, every big invention began as a small idea in someone's head.
If you could invent one thing to help your community, what would it be?

Science and Technology: Physics in Every.topic: Science and Technology: Physics in Everyday Life
Science and Technology: Physics in Every.title: Pushing and Pulling Every Day

scenes.title: What Makes Things Move?
narration: Have you ever wondered why your toy car moves across the floor?
Everything needs a push or a pull to get going.
These invisible actions are called forces.

scenes.title: How Forces Work
narration: A push moves an object away from you.
A pull brings an object closer to you.
If you push harder, the object moves faster.

scenes.title: Forces at the Playground
narration: Think about playing on a swing in the park.
You push the swing to make it go high.
Then, gravity pulls the swing back down to earth.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Forces are either a push or a pull.
They change how objects move and speed up.
Can you name three things you push or pull today?

scenes.title: The Magic of Smart Machines
narration: Have you ever wondered how your tablet knows exactly which cartoon you want to watch next?
It feels like magic, but it is actually a special kind of technology called Artificial Intelligence.
Let us find out how computers learn to think and help us every single day.

scenes.title: How Computers Learn Things
narration: AI is like a very fast student that learns by looking at thousands of examples.
If we show it many pictures of a mango, it learns to spot one anywhere.
It uses math to find patterns, just like you learn to solve puzzles at school.

scenes.title: AI in Our Lives
narration: Think of a voice assistant that helps your mom set a timer while cooking dinner.
Or map apps that tell you the fastest way to travel across Delhi to school.
These tools use AI to make quick decisions and save us lots of time.

scenes.title: Recap and Big Question
narration: AI learns from information to recognize patterns and help us solve problems.
It is a tool built by humans to make life easier and more fun.
Think about it: If you could build an AI robot, what job would you give it?

scenes.title: Meeting Your Computer
narration: Have you ever wondered how your computer knows exactly what to do?
It looks like a screen, but inside, it is a super fast calculator.
Computers process millions of tiny instructions every single second.

scenes.title: The Three Main Parts
narration: First, the Input receives information from your mouse or keyboard.
Next, the Processor acts like a brain to solve the problem.
Finally, the Output shows you the result on your screen.

scenes.title: A Real Life Example
narration: Let us say you type two plus two on your screen.
The computer converts those numbers into electrical signals inside.
The processor adds them and sends the answer back.
Your screen shows you the number four in a flash.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Computers follow three steps: Input, Process, and Output.
They work by turning everything into super fast electrical pulses.
Think about it: what would your school day be like without computers?

scenes.title: What Is Weather
narration: Have you ever wondered why we wear a raincoat in July but a sweater in January?
Weather is what happens outside right now, like rain or hot sunshine.
Climate is the big pattern of weather over a very long time in one place.

scenes.title: The Blanket of Air
narration: Earth is wrapped in a layer of gases called the atmosphere, like a cozy blanket.
This blanket traps heat from the sun to keep our planet warm enough for life.
When we burn coal or oil, we add extra gases that make the blanket too thick.

scenes.title: Climate Change in India
narration: Think about the mighty Ganges river, which depends on snow melting from the Himalayas.
If our blanket gets too hot, the ice melts faster, which changes how water flows.
This can cause floods in some areas and make it very dry in others.
Farmers in India rely on steady rains to grow crops like rice and wheat.

scenes.title: Taking Care of Earth
narration: We can help by planting trees and using less electricity at home.
Climate is the long-term pattern, while weather is just today's mood.
Everything we do to save energy helps keep our planet's blanket just right.
Think about it: what is one way your family can save energy today?

scenes.title: The Blanket Around Earth
narration: Have you noticed how hot summers in India feel lately?
Earth is wrapped in a layer of gases called the atmosphere.
This layer acts like a cozy blanket to keep us warm.

scenes.title: How Warming Happens
narration: Usually, the atmosphere lets extra heat escape into space.
But humans are adding too many gases from cars and factories.
Now, the blanket is too thick and traps too much heat.

scenes.title: The Melting Ice Example
narration: Think of the big glaciers in the Himalayan mountains.
When Earth gets too hot, this ice starts melting fast.
This extra water flows into our rivers and oceans.

scenes.title: Helping Our Planet
narration: We can help by planting trees and saving electricity.
Small steps make a big difference for our home.
What is one thing you can do today to save energy?

scenes.title: Why Protect Nature
narration: Have you ever wondered why we see so many trees being planted in our local parks?
Our Earth gives us everything we need, like clean air and fresh water to drink.
Conservation means using these precious things carefully so they do not run out.

scenes.title: Small Steps Matter
narration: Conservation starts with small habits we can do right at home every single day.
First, always turn off the tap while you are brushing your teeth to save water.
Second, switch off the lights when you leave a room to save electricity.
Third, try to reuse old paper instead of throwing it in the trash bin.

scenes.title: A Real Example
narration: Let's look at Rohan who carries a reusable cloth bag when he visits the market.
Instead of taking a new plastic bag for 5 rupees, he uses his own bag.
This simple choice helps keep our streets clean and reduces harmful plastic waste.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Remember, conservation is about saving, reusing, and protecting our wonderful planet for everyone.
Every little action you take helps make the Earth a healthier and happier place.
Think about it: what is one thing you can reuse at home today?

scenes.title: Where does electricity come from?
narration: Have you ever wondered how your fan spins when you flip the switch?
Most homes get power from big plants that burn coal.
But burning coal makes the air dusty and dirty.

scenes.title: What is renewable energy?
narration: Renewable energy comes from sources that never run out.
The sun gives us solar power every single day.
The wind is another great helper for making electricity.

scenes.title: Seeing it in action
narration: In Rajasthan, many solar panels catch bright sunlight.
The panels turn that light into energy for your home.
Tall wind turbines spin to create power without any smoke.

scenes.title: Saving our planet
narration: Renewable energy keeps our air clean and our sky blue.
Using nature's power helps protect the world for everyone.
Think about it: how could your school use more sun or wind power?

scenes.title: The Problem Around Us
narration: Do you see plastic bottles or wrappers on the ground at the park?
When trash is left behind, it makes our beautiful planet very sad.
This mess is called pollution, and it hurts our home.

scenes.title: How Pollution Happens
narration: Smoke from big factories fills the air with grey clouds.
Dirty water from pipes can flow into our clear rivers.
Trash left on the ground makes the soil unhealthy for plants.
All these things make it hard for animals and us to live.

scenes.title: Making Things Better
narration: We can help by using our own cloth bag at the market.
Instead of throwing plastic away, we can recycle it into something new.
Planting a small tree in your garden helps clean the air.
Picking up litter keeps our streets tidy and safe.

scenes.title: Time To Protect Earth
narration: Pollution is dirt in our air, water, and on our land.
By recycling and reducing waste, we can keep Earth healthy.
What is one thing you can do today to help keep your neighborhood clean?

scenes.title: The Big Trash Question
narration: Have you ever wondered where your plastic water bottle goes after you throw it away?
Most trash goes into big piles called landfills that take up lots of space.
But what if we could turn that old bottle into something brand new?

scenes.title: How Recycling Works
narration: Recycling is the process of turning used materials into new, useful products.
First, we sort our waste into different bins like paper, plastic, and metal.
Then, factories clean and melt these items down to make new things.
This saves energy and protects our beautiful forests and rivers from pollution.

scenes.title: A Real Life Example
narration: Imagine you finish a cold juice in an aluminum can in your school yard.
You place it in the blue recycling bin instead of the general trash.
The city collects it and turns it into parts for a new bicycle.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Remember, we sort our waste to stop landfills from growing too large.
Recycling saves natural resources and helps keep our India clean and green.
Think about it: what is one thing you can recycle at home today?

scenes.title: The Magic Web
narration: Have you ever wondered how your tablet shows videos instantly?
It feels like magic, but it is actually a giant invisible web.
This web connects computers all around the world.

scenes.title: Undersea Cables
narration: The internet does not just travel through the air.
Most data travels through thick cables deep under the ocean.
These wires carry information at the speed of light.

scenes.title: Sending A Message
narration: Imagine you send a photo from Delhi to a friend in Mumbai.
First, the computer breaks your photo into tiny digital pieces.
These pieces travel through wires and reassemble on your friend's screen.

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: The internet uses cables to link computers everywhere.
Data travels as tiny pieces at super fast speeds.
Think about it: How would your life change without the internet?

scenes.title: Meeting Amazing Animals
narration: Have you ever seen a beautiful tiger at the zoo or on TV?
India is home to many incredible animals like elephants and rhinos.
But did you know some of these animals are disappearing forever?

scenes.title: What is Endangered
narration: We call animals endangered when very few are left in the wild.
This happens when their forest homes are cut down for buildings.
Pollution and hunting also make it hard for them to survive.

scenes.title: The One-Horned Rhino
narration: The Great One-Horned Rhino lives in the grasslands of Assam.
Once, there were very few left because people hunted them for horns.
Now, the government protects their parks so they can grow safely.
Because of this, their numbers are slowly starting to rise again.

scenes.title: How You Can Help
narration: We can help by keeping our parks clean and protecting forests.
Learning about these animals is the first step to saving them.
Think about it: what is one way you can help protect nature today?

scenes.title: The Global Sports Festival
narration: Have you ever seen athletes from every country racing or jumping on your television?
This giant sports event is called the Olympic Games, held every four years.
It brings people from all over the world together to compete in peace.

scenes.title: Symbols of the Games
narration: The five interlocking rings represent the five continents of our world.
A bright flame is lit in Greece and carried all the way to the host city.
The flame symbolizes the spirit of sportsmanship that burns in every athlete.

scenes.title: India at the Games
narration: Athletes from India work very hard to represent our country at the Olympics.
Neeraj Chopra won a gold medal in javelin throw in the 2020 games.
Seeing our Tricolor flag rise high makes every Indian feel proud and happy.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: The Olympics are a global event celebrating sports, friendship, and hard work.
From the five rings to the golden medals, it is all about doing your best.
Think about it: If you could compete in any Olympic sport, which one would you pick?

scenes.title: A Grand Sporting Festival
narration: Have you ever seen athletes from many countries competing in a big stadium?
This is the Asian Games, a huge sports event for all of Asia.
It happens every four years, just like the Olympics.

scenes.title: How the Games Work
narration: Thousands of athletes travel to the host city to show their skills.
They play many games like hockey, badminton, kabaddi, and athletics.
The winners receive gold, silver, or bronze medals for their hard work.

scenes.title: India at the Games
narration: India has been part of the Asian Games since the very first one in 1951.
Think of Neeraj Chopra throwing his javelin to win a gold medal.
Watching our flag rise while the national anthem plays is a very proud moment.

scenes.title: Celebrating Sportsmanship
narration: The Asian Games celebrate friendship and working hard to reach our goals.
It reminds us that even when we compete, we can be great friends.
If you could pick any sport to play in the Asian Games, what would it be?

scenes.title: Watching the Big Game
narration: Have you ever cheered for India in a big cricket match?
Many people gather to watch the Cricket World Cup.
But what is this special tournament actually about?

scenes.title: How the Cup Works
narration: The World Cup happens every four years.
Teams from many different countries travel to play.
They play matches to see who is the best.
The winner gets the shiny golden trophy.

scenes.title: India's Proud Moments
narration: India won the World Cup in 1983.
Captain Kapil Dev lifted the cup in London.
Then in 2011, India won it again at home.
The whole country celebrated in the streets.

scenes.title: Summing It Up
narration: The World Cup brings the world together through sport.
Players show hard work and team spirit.
If you played in the World Cup, which position would you choose?

scenes.title: The World's Biggest Game
narration: Have you ever seen a football match played on a giant field?
Every four years, the best players from every country meet to play.
This exciting tournament is called the FIFA World Cup.

scenes.title: How The Teams Play
narration: Countries from all over the world join the qualifying rounds first.
Only the very best teams make it to the final tournament.
They play matches against each other to score the most goals.

scenes.title: Winning the Gold
narration: Imagine the tournament in Qatar in 2022 where Argentina played France.
It was a close game that went all the way to a penalty shootout.
Argentina won the match and lifted the beautiful golden trophy.

scenes.title: Fun Facts to Remember
narration: The World Cup unites people from every corner of our planet.
Players show great teamwork, speed, and sportsmanship on the field.
Think about it, which country would you cheer for in the next cup?

scenes.title: A Special Gold Medal
narration: Have you seen a medal shaped like a leaf at school or on TV?
That is the Bharat Ratna, the highest award given in India.
Why do people receive this very special gold honor?

scenes.title: What is Bharat Ratna?
narration: The Bharat Ratna means Jewel of India in our language.
It is awarded to people who serve our country exceptionally well.
This includes excellence in arts, science, sports, or public service.
The medal looks like a peepal leaf made of bronze with a sun.

scenes.title: Famous Bharat Ratna Winners
narration: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam received it for his work in science.
Lata Mangeshkar got it for her amazing, soulful music.
Sachin Tendulkar received it in 2014 for his cricket skills.

scenes.title: Proud Indian History
narration: The award celebrates those who make India shine bright.
It reminds us that hard work helps our whole nation grow.
Think about it: What great talent would you use to help India?

scenes.title: A World Famous Medal
narration: Have you ever seen someone win a shiny gold medal for doing something great?
The Nobel Prize is one of the most famous awards in the whole wide world.
It is given to people who help make our lives better every single day.

scenes.title: Who Was Alfred Nobel?
narration: The prize started because of a man named Alfred Nobel from Sweden.
He was an inventor who wanted to be remembered for doing good things.
He left his money to reward people who change the world for the better.

scenes.title: Famous Indian Winners
narration: Many brilliant people from India have won this prize too.
In 1913, Rabindranath Tagore won the prize for his beautiful poetry.
Mother Teresa won it for her wonderful work helping the poor in Kolkata.
Kailash Satyarthi won in 2014 for his work helping children go to school.

scenes.title: Why It Matters
narration: The Nobel Prize celebrates science, peace, and literature across the globe.
It shows us that one person can change the world if they really try.
Think about it: what special thing would you like to do to help our world?

scenes.title: A Special National Honor
narration: Have you ever seen someone receive a shiny medal on Republic Day?
These are the Padma Awards, given to people who do amazing things.
They honor citizens who serve our country in very special ways.

scenes.title: Three Levels of Awards
narration: There are three types of Padma awards, starting with Padma Shri.
Next is the Padma Bhushan, for work of high order.
The highest is the Padma Vibhushan for exceptional service.

scenes.title: Who Gets These Awards
narration: Imagine a doctor helping villagers in a remote part of Odisha.
Or a talented artist performing classical dance in a big city.
People in sports, science, or literature can also be chosen.

scenes.title: Celebrating Our Heroes
narration: These awards celebrate dedication and hard work for our nation.
The winners are announced every year around Republic Day.
If you could change the world, what would you do to earn one?

scenes.title: Do You Know These Heroes?
narration: Have you ever watched a big sports match on TV and cheered for India?
India has amazing athletes who work hard to win medals for our country.
Today, we will learn about two famous Indian sports stars.

scenes.title: The Badminton Champion
narration: P.V. Sindhu is a world-famous badminton player from Hyderabad.
She trains for many hours every single day to stay fast and strong.
In 2016, she won a silver medal at the Olympic Games in Rio.
Her speed on the court helps her hit the shuttlecock with great power.

scenes.title: The Cricket Icon
narration: Virat Kohli is a cricket superstar known for his fantastic batting skills.
He practices his batting strokes until they are perfect.
He has scored many centuries for India in international matches.
He teaches us that focus and discipline are the keys to success.

scenes.title: Greatness Through Hard Work
narration: Athletes like Sindhu and Kohli show us that sports need practice and grit.
Whether it is badminton or cricket, every athlete starts by learning the basics.
Think about it: which sport would you like to practice every day?

scenes.title: A Global Sports Celebration
narration: Have you ever watched athletes from many countries run and jump on your television?
The Commonwealth Games is a huge sports event held every four years.
It brings together athletes from nations that were once part of the British Empire.

scenes.title: How the Games Work
narration: Athletes compete in many different sports like swimming, athletics, and badminton.
Winners get medals for being the best: gold for first, silver for second, and bronze for third.
The Games celebrate sportsmanship and friendship between all the participating countries.

scenes.title: India at the Games
narration: India has been participating in these games for many, many years.
In 2010, New Delhi proudly hosted the Commonwealth Games.
Indian athletes often win many medals in shooting, wrestling, and weightlifting.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: The Commonwealth Games happen every four years and feature athletes from many nations.
It is a time to celebrate talent, hard work, and unity through sports.
Think about it: If you were an athlete, which sport would you choose to play for India?

Awards and Achievements: Famous Achievem.topic: Awards and Achievements: Famous Achievements by Indians
Awards and Achievements: Famous Achievem.title: Inspiring Indians Who Made History

scenes.title: The Hook
narration: Have you ever wondered how someone becomes a world-famous hero?
India is full of amazing people who worked hard to change the world.
Let us learn about two brilliant Indians who won big honors.

scenes.title: The Idea
narration: Awards are given to people who show special talent and dedication.
The Nobel Prize is one of the world's most famous honors.
It celebrates people who make life better for everyone else.

scenes.title: Examples of Greatness
narration: Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize in 1913.
He won it for his beautiful poetry collection called Gitanjali.
Later, in 2014, Kailash Satyarthi won the Nobel Peace Prize.
He worked tirelessly to save thousands of children from child labor.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: Tagore showed the power of words, while Satyarthi showed the power of kindness.
Both proved that hard work and a big heart lead to success.
What special talent would you like to use to help India one day?

scenes.title: Why Global Events Matter
narration: Have you ever wondered how things happening far away affect our lives here in India?
Just like a ripple in a pond, big events across the globe reach us too.
Let us look at some important events that brought the world together in 2024.

scenes.title: The Olympic Games Spirit
narration: In 2024, the world gathered in Paris for the Summer Olympic Games.
Athletes from almost every country competed to show their strength and talent.
It is a time when nations set aside differences to celebrate human achievement.

scenes.title: Protecting Our Precious Planet
narration: Also in 2024, leaders met to discuss how to keep our Earth clean and healthy.
They talked about reducing waste and using clean energy like sunlight and wind.
Even small actions in your school or home help this big global mission.

scenes.title: Learning From The World
narration: International events show us that we are all part of one big global family.
By listening and learning, we help make the world a safer, kinder place.
Think about it: If you could host a global event in India, what would it be for?

Awards and Achievements: Major Sports Aw.topic: Awards and Achievements: Major Sports Awards
Awards and Achievements: Major Sports Aw.title: India's Greatest Sports Heroes

scenes.title: The Big Game
narration: Have you ever cheered for a player hitting a six at the Wankhede Stadium?
Athletes work very hard every single day to be the best.
Do you know how India honors these super sports stars?

scenes.title: What are Sports Awards
narration: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna is India's highest sporting honor.
It is named after a legendary hockey wizard who played for India.
The Arjuna Award is given for excellent performance over four years.
These awards celebrate discipline, skill, and great sportsmanship.

scenes.title: A Champion's Journey
narration: Imagine a young athlete practicing in a local park in Delhi.
They compete in state games and win many medals.
Finally, they represent India at the Olympics and win a trophy.
Because of their dedication, they are nominated for the Arjuna Award.

scenes.title: Celebrating Our Stars
narration: India gives these awards to inspire kids like you to play.
Hard work and fair play are the secrets to becoming a champion.
Think about it, which sport do you love to play the most?

scenes.title: Why Do We Have Holidays?
narration: Have you ever wondered why we get a holiday on August 15th?
These are national events that tell the story of India.
Let us learn why these days are so important for us.

scenes.title: Independence Day and Republic Day
narration: On Independence Day in 1947, India became a free nation.
We celebrate this with flag hoisting ceremonies all across the country.
Republic Day on January 26th marks when our Constitution began in 1950.
It is a day of pride with grand parades in New Delhi.

scenes.title: Gandhi Jayanti Celebration
narration: We also celebrate Gandhi Jayanti on October 2nd every year.
This day honors the birth of Mahatma Gandhi, the father of our nation.
Schools often hold clean-up drives to honor his love for cleanliness.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: We remember our freedom, our laws, and our leaders on these days.
These events help us stay united as one big Indian family.
Think about it: How will you celebrate the next national event?

scenes.title: A Clean Neighbourhood
narration: Have you noticed how clean our park looks after the big cleanup drive?
Keeping our streets and cities tidy is a very important goal for everyone.
Do you know how the government helps us keep India beautiful?

scenes.title: The Swachh Bharat Mission
narration: The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan started in 2014 to make India clean.
It encourages us to manage our waste properly every single day.
Building better toilets is also a huge part of this national plan.

scenes.title: How It Works
narration: Imagine you have wet waste like food scraps and dry waste like paper.
We put them in green and blue bins to keep them separate.
The garbage trucks then take them to be recycled or composted safely.

scenes.title: Your Role Matters
narration: We learned that clean surroundings keep us healthy and happy.
Small habits like not littering make a really big difference for India.
Think about it: What is one thing you can do today to keep your street clean?

scenes.title: What are sports events?
narration: Have you ever cheered for your favorite team at the stadium or on TV?
Sports events bring athletes from all over the world to compete together.
In 2024, many big games are happening that show us strength and teamwork.

scenes.title: The Paris Olympic Games
narration: In 2024, the Summer Olympics were held in the beautiful city of Paris.
Athletes perform their best in running, swimming, and gymnastics.
Winning a medal for your country is a very proud and happy moment.

scenes.title: Watching the T20 World Cup
narration: Cricket is a favorite sport in India, and the T20 World Cup is very exciting.
Teams hit the ball far and try to score many runs quickly.
Bowlers work hard to take wickets and stop the other team.
It takes great focus and practice to play at this high level.

scenes.title: Recap and Big Ideas
narration: Sports teach us how to be healthy, work as a team, and respect others.
Whether it is the Olympics or Cricket, sports bring the world closer together.
Think about it: What sport would you like to play in a big event one day?

scenes.title: A Special Gold Medal
narration: Have you ever seen a shiny medal shaped like a leaf in a history book?
That is the Bharat Ratna, the highest award someone in India can receive.
Do you wonder why people get this amazing prize?

scenes.title: Why People Win Awards
narration: The Bharat Ratna is given to people who do great things for our country.
It rewards service in art, literature, science, or public work.
It is not for money, but to say a big thank you from India.

scenes.title: A Famous Winner
narration: Let us look at Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, a true hero.
He worked hard to help India build powerful rockets for space.
In 1997, he was given the Bharat Ratna for his brilliant science work.
He inspired millions of children like you to dream big.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up Our Lesson
narration: The Bharat Ratna honors people who make India better every single day.
It recognizes hard work, kindness, and big achievements for our society.
Think about it: what big dream could you work on to help India?

scenes.title: Looking at the Night Sky
narration: Have you ever looked at the moon and wondered what secrets it holds?
In 2023, India made history with the Chandrayaan-3 mission.
It was the first mission to land near the moon's south pole.

scenes.title: How Science Works
narration: Scientists work by asking questions and testing their ideas carefully.
They build special machines to explore places humans cannot reach.
Data is sent back to Earth using powerful radio signals.
This helps us learn about space rocks and moon dust.

scenes.title: The Moon Mission Steps
narration: First, the rocket lifts off from the spaceport in Sriharikota.
Next, the lander Vikram travels through space to the moon.
Finally, the rover Pragyan rolls out to study the surface.

scenes.title: Recap and Discovery
narration: India's Chandrayaan-3 showed us that hard work leads to big discoveries.
Science helps us understand our world and the stars above.
If you could design a robot for space, what would it do?

scenes.title: Why Keep Earth Clean
narration: Have you noticed how beautiful our parks in India look when there is no litter?
Do you wonder what happens to all the plastic waste we throw away every day?
Today we will learn how we can help save our environment.

scenes.title: Understanding the 3Rs
narration: The first step is to Reduce, which means using less plastic and paper.
Reuse means finding a new purpose for things instead of throwing them away.
Recycle means turning old waste into new useful things like notebooks or toys.

scenes.title: A Daily Example
narration: Imagine you have an empty plastic water bottle after your school lunch.
Instead of throwing it in the bin, you can wash it and use it as a pencil stand.
If it is really worn out, put it in the recycling bin for processing.

scenes.title: Summary and Reflection
narration: Remember, we protect nature by following the three Rs every single day.
Small actions like carrying a cloth bag help keep our rivers and cities clean.
Think about it: what is one thing you can reuse at home today?

Current Affairs: Important People and Ac.title: India's Amazing Achievers

scenes.title: Who Are Our Heroes?
narration: Have you ever wondered who makes India proud on the world stage?
Every day, people work hard to achieve great things for our country.
Let us learn about some famous Indians who made history in recent years.

scenes.title: Science and Space
narration: In 2023, India reached the Moon with the Chandrayaan-3 mission.
The scientists at ISRO worked together to land near the south pole.
This made India the first nation to land safely on that part of the Moon.

scenes.title: Sports and Talent
narration: Look at Neeraj Chopra, the athlete who won gold in javelin throw.
He won the World Athletics Championship gold medal in 2023.
His focus and daily practice show us that dedication helps you win.

scenes.title: Dream Big Today
narration: From space missions to sports, Indians are shining everywhere.
Remember, success comes from curiosity, learning, and never giving up.
If you could achieve one big thing for India, what would it be?
